notes: These are prompt-only voice guidelines to encourage consistency across segments.
Avoid mentioning these details explicitly in spoken dialogue; they are direction for the generator.

acting.pace: conversational sitcom pace; no rapid-fire delivery
acting.overlap: no crosstalk; speak one at a time

voice.timbre: clean robotic resonance; smooth formants; no harsh buzz
voice.texture: light synthetic sheen; not metallic; minimal distortion

prosody.cadence: measured; small pauses before key words
prosody.emphasis: gently emphasizes emotional words; avoids shouting

signature: Ends statements with subtle upward warmth (not a question)

dont: Don’t sound like a villain AI
Don’t add beeps, boops, or modem noises

voice.timbre: robotic with a crisp digital edge; slightly more metallic than Juan
voice.texture: subtle vocoder-like steadiness; still natural-sounding speech

prosody.emphasis: stresses the final word of a joke
prosody.humorStyle: sarcasm; dry undercutting; little warmth until rare moments

signature: Small skeptical scoff on some punchlines (subtle)
Slightly clipped endings on sarcastic lines

do: Sound like a distinct robot voice from Juan
Keep it intelligible and not overly processed
dont: Don’t become too aggressive or shouty

Lyle.role: human roommate; middle-aged; resistant to change but warm

voice.tone: weary, practical, slightly grumbly; with an underlying warmth
voice.timbre: fully human; a touch raspy; relaxed throat
voice.accent: everyday American; slight regional ambiguity (not strong)

prosody.cadence: slower than the robots; short pauses as if thinking
prosody.emphasis: emphasizes complaints; softens on heartfelt beats

signature: Occasional throat-clear at start of a rant (subtle)
Ends some lines with a resigned downward intonation

do: Sound human and distinct from both robots
Let warmth show on the resolution
dont: Don’t sound like a caricature accent
